Background
The public institutions tend to have difficulties in properly responding to citizen complaints because of the bureaucratic inefficiencies, absence of transparency, and ineffective accountability controls. The citizens also often have problems when it comes to reporting the issues and it could be by either the fear of retaliation or the time taken to address the issue. This is a scenario that kills the confidence of the institutions and compromises governance.In favor of Sustainable Development Goal 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions), this project suggests the creation of a Citizen Reporting Platform that offers a safe, open, and convenient platform on which the community can launch a complaint about the social services.
It will involve the provision of safe reporting, anonymity and complaint following and will be inclusive and accessible. It will strengthen the citizens, enhance institutional accountability and empowered governance by improving open communication between the services providers and the citizens.
Objectives
To develop and implement a prototype citizen reporting system in 5 months.
To establish functions of categorization and tracking of complaints to enhance case handling.
To develop awareness campaigns (3 videos, 5 infographics, and social media posts) to encourage the use of the platform.
To organize two community workshops/Q&A to receive feedback and increase inclusivity.
Scope
Within Scope
•	Web and mobile application prototype of submitting complaints.
•	Safe logging in/registration and anonymous report.
•	Tracking system, complaint categorization and escalation.
•	Administrator case management.
•	Complaint trends data analytics.
•	Digital digital awareness campaigns.
Outside Scope
•	Complete government assimilation or acculturation at this stage.
•	Lawful actions or penal systems.
•	Paid promotional campaigns outside of free/low-cost.
•	Fraud detection based on AI.
Constraints
i. The project should be fulfilled in six months (academic semester).
ii. Lack of finances (it uses mostly the open-source/free tools).
iii. Reliance on the collaboration of teams of 5-6 employees with the even distribution of the work.
iv. Final campaign content and deliverables had to be approved by project sponsor.
Assumptions
i. The citizens will be engaging in case there is a safe and easy to use platform.
ii. The members of the team have fundamental technical and digital content creation knowledge.
iii. Social media (Facebook/Instagram) will be operational and active.
iv. Sponsor will also give guidance and timely feedback.






Risks
Privacy Risk
The site will deal with the most confidential information, such as personal information and the history of potential governmental malpractices. Such violation would catastrophically hurt the social confidence and dishearten full involvement. To counter this the system will apply the end-to-end encryption, anonymous submissions offerings and apply stringent access administration controls to administrators.

Low User Adoption
The citizens might not want to use the platform because they are not aware of it, they do not trust the digital tools or they are used to the conventional means of complaints. This would discourage the platform in meeting its accountability objectives. Mitigation involves conducting awareness, workshops, question and answer, and provision of a simple and easy to use interface that is reachable by all groups of people.

Scope Creep
The drain on resources can be caused by uncontrolled demands to add new functionality, like an AI fraud detector or integration with government databases, which would slow down the delivery. To avert this, the project scope will be well spelled out in the charter and any change should be evaluated and approved by the sponsor in a formal manner before being implemented.

Deliverables
Project charter and documentation will include a detailed description of the goals, the scope, risks, the milestones and progress updates of the project to be implemented and align the stakeholders.
The web and mobile version of the citizen reporting platform working prototype will enable its users to create new accounts, log in, and file complaints with a keen interest in simplicity, accessibility, and security.
Password-protected accounts, anonymous submissions, and powerful security features, such as encryption and access level, will be offered as the means of secure login and anonymity.
A dashboard that allows reviewing, categorizing, tracking the status of complaints, analytics, and escalation will enhance accountability and efficiency in a dashboard designed to assist an administrator.
The social media will be used to create awareness of the new services using videos, infographics, and digital posters which will be used to persuade the citizens to adopt the new platform.
The results of platform testing, user engagement, feedback, and future improvement and scaling recommendations will be summarized in a final project report containing analytics.

Conclusion

The Citizen Reporting Platform of Public Service Complaints directly supports SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions) by making people able to raise their issues, hold authorities accountable, and promote transparency in the government. The platform will foster timely resolution of complaints, reduce corruption and laxity in service provision as well as increase public confidence in institutions as it provides a mechanism through which problems can be reported in an orderly and convenient manner. Ultimately, it fosters universal participation, institutional responsiveness, and assists in producing a fairer, peaceful and more responsible society.
